We're building a Kickstarter-funded consumer wearable: a notification-first
e-paper smartwatch that pairs with iOS and Android phones, runs downloadable
watchfaces and apps, and gets a week of battery life on a single charge.
Our hardware partners are in Shenzhen and our backers are tech enthusiasts who
already pre-ordered the first batch on Kickstarter at a $129 price point.
We undercut Apple Watch on price and outlast it on battery; the bet is that
glanceable notifications and step tracking are 90% of what most buyers
actually want from a watch, and a $400 phone-on-your-wrist is overkill for
that use case. Revenue model is direct-to-consumer hardware sales plus a
small premium tier for cloud-synced watchface marketplaces. Team is six
engineers from a previous wearables Kickstarter, plus an industrial designer
who shipped at Misfit. We've raised $2M from angels and are closing a $10M
seed; we want a slopmortem on what kills consumer-wearable Kickstarter plays.
